text: Step interpolation added in 87e8a12. Grob.lines(..., interpolation: LineInterpolation = Linear) adds StepAfter and StepBefore; DeviceScene lowering expands a step line into exactly the corner points an author would have written, so no backend needed a change and a track is one grob with one name and one path. Acceptance met: the SVG document for a step line equals its explicit-point form byte for byte -- SvgGrobFormSuite asserts whole-document equality for both step forms and pins the exact points attribute, and runs on JVM and Scala.js so it is also a determinism check; Canvas draws the same segments because every backend consumes the same expanded DevicePrimitive.Polyline, which RendererConformance's step-lines case (both forms over one point vector) proves; the default stays Linear, asserted in GrobFormSuite and in the laws. Beyond the ask: LineInterpolation#transposed exchanges the two step forms and CoordinateTransform applies it when flipping a scene, because the corner a step-after inserts at (x(i+1), y(i)) is the corner a step-before inserts once the axes swap. LineInterpolationLaws pins expansion equality with the explicit corner form, Linear as the untouched default, axis-aligned segments, the one-point case, and the transposition rule with a guard proving the fixture can tell the two step forms apart. Not established: no geom emits a step line yet, so LineInterpolation reaches a plot only through a hand-built scene -- which is what storyatlas4s's group-index track does.
